title: Volcan: hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff
status: Plan for the re-take on the live build, not recorded. The narration is measured by video/generate-narration.py, and the cold open and the product windows of beats 4 and 5 by a free rehearsal of 2026-10-06 against a local server. Beat 2's window is sized from the 25 s model timeout and the Amazon Bedrock answer that take 3 measured on the live build on 2026-10-06; only the headline-length allowance in it is an ESTIMATE. video/SHOT_LIST.md is the plan in full.
previous_take_script: The 2026-09-29 render of 09d4862 used the six-beat script at commit fc10e7d: git show fc10e7d:video/narration.json
timing_basis: Measured: each beat's narration by video/generate-narration.py (ElevenLabs audio, measured with ffprobe) plus the generator's 0.65 s tail and the beat's product window. The video opens on a 2.0 s title card, then the cold open of cold_open.seconds, then beat 1, so every beat timestamp below is offset by cards.title_seconds plus cold_open.seconds. Each product window names its own basis.

narration_audio.note: Not generated for this plan. video/generate-narration.py --write-timestamps replaces every timestamp here with measured values.

cold_open.basis: Measured on 2026-10-06 against a local server on port 8813 with no cloud credentials, on upgradedev/volcan-demo-service pull request 1: the typed command line 26 took 12.03, 12.04 and 11.88 s from Enter to the browser's speech end event for its readback and answer. Typing starts 0.1 s into the cold open and Enter follows about 0.3 s later. The slowest run plus 1 s plus that lead, rounded up to the half second. The turn reads the parsed patch and calls no model, so its words are the same on the live build. Findings took 29.8 s and Summary 24.6 s and 24.5 s on the same server, against the capture's 20 s cap for a cold open; on the live build Summary also speaks the model's headline, up to 180 characters, after the finding.
cold_open.visual_action: After the 2.0 s title card. The chosen pull request was opened on the live page before the camera rolled, because opening one runs the default engine, an Amazon Bedrock call, and one live digest took 19.67 s on 2026-10-01; the band says so, and says that the pull request is a demo written for this walkthrough. The first frame is the dialogue under Talk through a real pull request, showing the opened overview. Within the first 0.5 s, Alt and 4 puts the focus in the command box, line 26 is typed and Enter sends it. The page speaks its readback, Understood: line 26., then the line: Line 6 of 9, added, new line 26: return user.role not equals Role.ADMIN, the inverted comparison in is_admin, and the dialogue log prints the line with != under the overview, which says 2 security findings. The review card that names the finding, an authorization comparison was inverted, is not in this frame; the capture checks that the turn's answer carries it. The turn reads the report already built and calls no model. The narrator is silent. The product's own voice is in the mix for the whole turn.
cold_open.gate: The first product sound by 2.0 s after the title card ends, which is 4.0 s into the video, and the first spoken word by 5.0 s into the video, which is 3.0 s into the cold open with the 2.0 s card. The turn plays to its end with nothing over it. A take that misses either is recorded again.

{build} at commit {sha7}. Simulated Alexa+ front end. GitHub review: dry run.

beats.narration_text: Volcan, built for Alexa+, lets blind and low-vision developers review AI code by voice.
beats.speech_text: Volcan, built for Alexa plus, lets blind and low-vision developers review A I code by voice.
beats.visual_action: The cold-open turn has ended. The view scrolls to the top of the live page: the heading Hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff, For blind and low-vision developers, the silent preview of the Inverted admin check patch, and the label Live MCP server, simulated Alexa+ front end. Not an Alexa skill. GitHub: dry-run. That label stays on screen; the narration does not open with it. Late in the line, Alt and 1 puts the focus ring on Hear this code review. No product turn in this beat.

beats.narration_text: Press once, and this patch goes to Amazon Bedrock.
beats.speech_text: Press once, and this patch goes to Amazon Bedrock.
beats.product_sound_basis: Measured on the live build, except a 0.5 s headline allowance (ESTIMATE). The press is made when the narrator stops, after the generator's 0.65 s tail, so this window runs from the press and the answer can only start after the narration. It holds a call that runs to the 25 s timeout (MODEL_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC in src/infrastructure/bedrock_adapter.py; past it the server falls back to the local engine and the take is recorded again), then the answer as take 3 measured it on the live build on 2026-10-06: the falling earcon, which starts 0.65 s before the first word, and the sentence SemanticDiffReport.to_voice_summary(level=0) builds, the finding, then the model's headline, then the counts, which spoke for 31.42 s (from no later than 13.906 s to 45.328 s of timeline) with a 173-character headline. shorten_for_speech caps the headline at 180 characters; the 7 more characters are about 0.5 s. The local engine's sentence, finding and counts only, took 16.75 s in the rehearsal of 2026-10-06. 25 + 0.65 + 31.42 + 0.5 = 57.57 s, rounded up to the half second: 58.0 s, which leaves 0.43 s for the request's round trip outside the model call. In take 3 the answer's first sound came about 4.3 s after the press; any call from about 2 s to the timeout only moves the silent hold after the answer.
beats.visual_action: The narrator says one line and stops. After the generator's 0.65 s tail, Enter on Hear this code review, where Alt and 1 put the focus in beat 1: the model call starts only now, so its answer cannot start under the narration. The silent preview stays drawn and the button shows it is working. No cut and no speed-up: the wait is shown as it happened. When the answer arrives, the page plays the falling earcon the server returned and speaks the server's sentence, the finding, then the model's headline, then the counts, while the words light. The product's own sound and voice are in the mix and nothing talks over them. A fast answer leaves the page holding, silent, until beat 3. The engine meter must read Amazon Bedrock; a take whose meter reads local heuristic, or that shows a fallback reason, is recorded again.

beats.narration_text: Amazon Bedrock answered Volcan on AWS Lambda, with DynamoDB. That's how much it read.
beats.speech_text: Amazon Bedrock answered Volcan on A W S Lambda, with Dynamo D B. That's how much it read.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the engine meter reading Amazon Bedrock and the round trip the page measured while the narrator names Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda and DynamoDB. On the second sentence, the coverage line under the spoken caption, exactly as the page prints it: for this short patch, The model read the whole N-character patch., with N as printed. Then open the details The model's full answer and hold on the model's own words. Nothing is typed over the page; every number on screen is one the page printed.

beats.narration_text: Request changes stages a review, bound to the head commit it read.
beats.speech_text: Request changes stages a review, bound to the head commit it read.
beats.product_sound_basis: Measured on 2026-10-06 against a local server on port 8813 with no cloud credentials, on upgradedev/volcan-demo-service pull request 1 with the review comment is_admin is inverted.: 25.39, 25.45 and 25.28 s from the click on Request changes to the browser's speech end event for its readback and answer. The slowest run plus 1 s, rounded up to the half second. The readback and the answer both repeat the comment, so a longer comment needs a longer window: the 69-character comment this replaces took 33.4 s.
beats.visual_action: Back to Talk through a real pull request, where the chosen pull request is still open. The review comment is_admin is inverted. goes into the comment box, and Request changes after the narrator stops (or the command request changes followed by that comment, typed with Alt and 4). The page plays its cue and speaks its readback, then Ready to request changes on the pull request, bound to head commit and its first seven characters, with the comment, then Say confirm to submit it, or cancel. State AWAITING CONFIRM, with Confirm and Cancel outlined. The whole turn is in the mix as the product's voice; nothing talks over it.

beats.narration_text: Nothing leaves Volcan until you confirm. Confirm, and listen.
beats.speech_text: Nothing leaves Volcan until you confirm. Confirm, and listen.
beats.product_sound_basis: Measured on 2026-10-06 against a local server on port 8813 with no cloud credentials, on upgradedev/volcan-demo-service pull request 1, each time after Request changes with the comment is_admin is inverted.: 22.28, 22.28, 22.27, 22.21 and 23.41 s from the click on Confirm to the browser's speech end event for its readback and answer. The slowest run plus 1 s, rounded up to the half second. Confirm calls no model, so the live build speaks the same sentences.
beats.visual_action: Confirm after the narrator stops. The page plays its cue and speaks Understood: confirm., then Dry run. Nothing was sent to GitHub. The head commit is still the commit it read, and the exact request Volcan would send has been recorded. A live send would be refused: no GITHUB_TOKEN is set. State RECORDED, NOT SENT. Midway the view moves to the review pane: outcome recorded and not sent, the live head re-read, and the exact POST request body the server recorded. Nothing talks over the turn.

beats.narration_text: No GitHub token here: the request is recorded, not sent.
beats.speech_text: No GitHub token here: the request is recorded, not sent.
beats.visual_action: The page has stopped speaking. Hold on the review pane the view moved to during Confirm: outcome recorded and not sent, the live head re-read, and the exact POST request body the server recorded. No product turn in this beat. The screencast ends on this narration, so its sound reaches to within the generator's 0.65 s tail of beat 7, as the sync gate's content-seam check needs: a window that ends on the page's own speech ends in silence, because the slowest-plus-1-s rule leaves a margin and the re-rendered system voice ends before the browser's.

beats.narration_text: This MCP handshake is real. Alexa+ never called Volcan.
beats.speech_text: This M C P handshake is real. Alexa plus never called Volcan.
beats.visual_action: Evidence, tab Server and MCP: Server reached, with the commit and the model path the live server reports. On the first sentence press Run a real MCP handshake, which sends initialize and tools/list and calls no tool, and hold on the negotiated version 2025-11-25 and the tool list as the page prints them. On the last sentence the connection strip and its Alexa+ box, which reads package built and tested locally, not certified or deployed. Then the closing card. Do not press Replay the documented Alexa+ requests on the live build: each of its three clients calls digest_semantic_diff with the default engine, so one press is three billed Bedrock calls and could run close to a minute.
